slides: In the last question, choosing the hundreds digit also decided the units digit. That idea deserves a closer look.

slides.say: When one choice forces another, the forced position gets exactly one option. Let's see it in three examples.
How many four-digit numbers have all their digits the same?
The first digit can't be zero, so it's one to nine. Nine options.
And the second digit? You might think nine options too. It could be one, in one one one one. Or two, in two two two two.
But that's not really true. Once the first digit is chosen, the others must be the same digit. If we pick five, the number is five five five five. So each of the other positions gets one option.
at: So each of the other positions

slides.say: Nine times one times one times one is nine.
Here they are, one one one one, two two two two, up to nine nine nine nine. Just nine numbers.
Careful, not nine to the power of four. That would let every digit be anything.
at: not nine to the power of four

slides.say: Now a new example. How many four-digit numbers have the same first digit and last digit?
The first digit, one to nine. Nine options.
at: The first digit, one to nine

slides.say: The second and third digits have no restriction. Each one has ten options, zero included.
And the last digit must copy the first. One option. So choosing the first digit really chooses two digits.
Nine times ten times ten times one is nine hundred.
And one zero zero one counts too, so don't drop the zero from the middle.
One more example. Four-digit numbers like three three seven seven, where the second digit copies the first, and the fourth copies the third.
The first digit, one to nine, nine options. The second copies it, one option.
The third digit is free, zero to nine, ten options. The fourth copies it, one option.
Nine times one times ten times one is ninety. From one one zero zero, up to nine nine nine nine.
So let's sum it up. A forced position gets one option.
Count each free choice once, and the copies get one. Take a moment to memorize this, and I'll see you in the next video.
